europe4.notes:
Hillwood Reguły location resolution — 28 October 2026

One proposed physical campus and one planned service-complex project. Base hundredfifth: 862 sites / 930 projects. Build and validate-only pass: 863 sites / 931 projects / 66 countries / 4858 evidence rows. All five selected-base tables show no matching identity. Earlier Reguły hold is the same lead and is resolved; no earlier packet was edited.

The exact chain is independently reviewable without image registration:

- Municipal ruling OŚ.6220.18.2023, dated 2 October 2026, page 1, explicitly identifies HE4 Warsaw 4’s planned data-storage service complex 3 in Reguły, full parcel 385 and parts of ten neighbouring parcels. September 4 ruling pages 11–12 explicitly describes the server-room, backup generation and cooling scope; page 3 links the other three service-complex proceedings.
- Official KRS 0000530590 names HE4 Warsaw 4 and its sole shareholder EU Industrial Club IV Société en Commandite Spéciale. Official UOKiK describes that company as part of Hillwood. UOKiK’s Zgorzelec transaction is corporate-identity evidence only, never Reguły location/status. Hillwood’s September 15 release separately identifies the four-building Reguły commercial data-centre campus.
- The ULDK response explicitly returns Michałowice / Reguły / 142104_2.0013.385 and the WGS84 polygon. The area centroid [20.8701088,52.1751607] is verified inside it. It is a derived interior marker in one fully named project parcel, not a published point, building centroid or entire-campus boundary. Horizontal accuracy remains unknown.

October 2 pauses the environmental decision procedure until submission of the mandatory EIA report. It does not say physical construction was underway or paused. Status is announced as of October 2 for service complex 3. No permit-to-build, start, completed, operating, capacity or operator claim is added. The other three campus components remain context rather than invented project records.

The Europe 3 affine fits, manually guessed point and parcel 562/4 remain rejected. No derived coordinate or control from them enters this packet. Exact primary parcels resolve this independently. The current municipal index, September/October rulings and scoped web searches revealed no subsequent project-specific start, permission, cancellation, relocation or operation. The precise October 2 body date is used; retrieval and generic page dates are not lifecycle evidence.

Six admitted sources and fourteen raw capture/metadata pairs are pinned in sources.json and capture-manifest.json. Extra municipal searches and the developer privacy page are retained as research context only. PDF page 1 was rendered and visually read to confirm applicant, parcel list and procedural wording. Prior files, source definitions, datasets and tracked files were not edited.

americas4.notes:
# TGRU1 bounded locator pass — 28 October 2026

One ready candidate, pending independent geometry review. Base hundredfifth has 862 sites / 930 projects. Final build and validate-only pass to 863 / 931 / 66 countries, with four new evidence records. All previous site/project rows and the imported source and identity snapshots remain unchanged. Americas3 and all tracked files were preserved.

The 3 September 2026 original Tecto post explicitly says TGRU1 is currently under construction in Santana de Parnaíba. Its JSON-LD timestamp is 2026-09-03T19:35:58.245Z. Status is retained at that date, with no building-stage, completed-capacity or opening inference. The current undated operator page is identity/successor context only. Planned 200 MW is not IT load or achieved supply.

Municipal CONDEMAS 73rd-meeting pages 10–14 identify Aurea Finvest / Tectodigital III (CNPJ 57.212.918/0001-11), process 250.528.049.625.300, Estrada da Bela Vista, Tanquinho and merged glebas 11–16. The company legal suffix III is not interpreted as TGRU3; the operator's named Santana de Parnaíba development is TGRU1. This identity bridge is explicitly contextual, rather than a source directly equating the code with the legal company name. Page 11 shows the Tecto area and three schematic buildings; page 14 shows the project outline on a surrounding-road map. The additional municipal resolution capture is retained as context, not admitted as a fresh permit or construction source.

The page 14 embedded image was extracted without resampling using pdfimages. It is 846 × 498 pixels, file plan14-003.png. No usable source CRS or PDF georeferencing dictionary was found. Five manually selected surrounding road nodes from the raw OSM API XML provide an affine registration. They span the map, including the distinct Lula Chaves reverse bend, its Estrada do Engenho junction, the Bela Vista access junction, the residential loop, and the eastern Lula Chaves/Pentágono junction. The eastern road names differ from the SABESP prose's broader network connection description; matching uses actual road shapes and intersections, not a claim that the utility endpoint is the campus.

Final control fit RMS is 6.93 m; individual control residuals are 1.27–13.13 m. Two unused checkpoints differ by 5.75 m and 10.54 m. Dropping one control at a time moves the selected point by 1.13–22.00 m. The fifth control was added after the initial four-control fit showed poor leave-one-out conditioning; the final five-control fit and diagnostics supersede that trial. All source control pixels, exact OSM node IDs and coordinates, affine coefficients, unused checks and sensitivity results are in geometry-facts.json. The rendered registration-overlay.png shows the transformed complete road network over the source plan; the selected point is cyan. Controls are numbered red.

The chosen source pixel [300, 190] maps to longitude -46.9039066, latitude -23.4519391. It is about 34.5 source pixels / 68 m inside the visible yellow project outline. The western end of the project outline is clipped by the source image, so the hand-traced visible outline is only a containment/margin aid, not a complete cadastral polygon. No boundary is emitted. The point is a derived campus locator with compiled authority and georeferenced_source_map derivation. Fit residuals are not absolute or surveyed accuracy, and horizontal uncertainty remains unknown. No individual data-hall or substation position is asserted.

All five hundredfifth base files, tracked holds and available local changes/holds were searched. Prior holds refer to the same TGRU1 project; Bela Vista matches include the unrelated Elea POA1 address in Porto Alegre. The nearest selected existing site is ODATA SP01, approximately 1.2 km away. No ODATA point, city centre, utility endpoint or broad industrial-estate locator was reused.

The primary operator page and bounded searches found no later physical-status successor. Existing failed routes were not repeatedly retried: prior DataCenterMap HTTP 429 remains excluded; this pass retains an Overpass HTTP 406 and a timeout, then uses the normal public OSM map API successfully. Esri imagery and the operator rendering are supplemental visual context, not the status source or registration basis. Raw captures are ignored and hash checked; none are proposed for redistribution.
